short_answer: Rob Veno is a real, active product on WagerTalk, a Las Vegas pick marketplace with written terms and a mailing address. His profile prices every package, shows a table of his last 20 graded plays and lists his radio and newsletter history. In that narrow sense the service is legitimate.

Whether the picks make money over time is a separate question, and nothing we could open answers it. The sales copy leads with runs such as "CFB + NFL L9W = +69.7 units, 59.4% (82-56-0)" and "NFL Playoffs L3Y = OUTSTANDING 45-25", each over a window the seller chose. His Last 20 table was strong on 17 Nov 2026 at 14 wins and 6 losses, but that covers only three days.

We found no independent buyer post about his paid picks, good or bad. The CapperTek reviews of WagerTalk that we read describe losing after purchase, but none of them names him. Treat the numbers as marketing until you have tracked his picks yourself.

guarantee: WagerTalk sells many daily picks in two versions: a plain price and a higher "Guaranteed" price (the same site rule applies to his daily picks, though none was on sale when we checked). The profile says the guarantee "backs your purchase with 100% in credits." If the daily package does not show an overall profit across all included plays, the paid cash value is credited to your WagerTalk account for a future purchase. It is not cash back.

The WagerTalk refund policy says "All Sales are Final" and that no refunds will be issued once a product is purchased, delivered or viewed. The terms limit the company's entire liability to a refund of the price paid or a replacement, at the company's option. We saw no guarantee on the multi day or season passes. Nothing covers losses on the bets themselves, which are usually far larger than the package price.

claims_note: Each run covers a window the seller picked, such as the last nine weeks (L9W), the last six weeks of a season (L6W) or the last three years of playoffs (L3Y). None of them is a full season or career record, and units depend on how big each play was rated.

The bio says he was invited to the Stardust Invitational in 1996 and 2004 and the Sunset Station Invitational in 2000, co-hosted a radio show from 1992 and was a mainstay of the Sportsmemo radio show from 1998. We did not check these with outside records.
His Last 20 table, graded by WagerTalk, showed 14 wins and 6 losses for plays dated 14 Nov to 16 Nov 2026. Twenty plays in three days is a very short sample.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every Rob Veno pick kept by a third party, no contest results we could open, and no court or regulator record about him.

What the seller publishes: a Last 20 table, a Hot Streaks box and Who's Hot leaderboards. On 17 Nov 2026 the Last 20 table showed 14 wins and 6 losses across college basketball, NBA, NFL, CFL and college football, most of them totals. One leaderboard block showed him at 18-10 for the last 30 days. All of these are graded by WagerTalk, the company that sells the picks.

He also posts free picks with written analysis, and the WagerTalk account on X announces them several times a week. Free picks are a fair way to judge his reasoning, but a handful of them is not a record.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no pick history from Rob Veno is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Rob Veno performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the runs on his WagerTalk profile sit at about 59% to 64% winners. On the Watchdog board on 17 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence about Rob Veno is close to nonexistent. Most public posts that name him are WagerTalk's own free pick announcements. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found no independent post from anyone who bought Rob Veno picks, positive or negative. The posts that name him are WagerTalk's free pick announcements and TheRX forum rules, which bar members from posting his plays along with many other paid services. CapperTek reviews of WagerTalk from 2021 to 2026 describe losing after purchase, but none of the ones we read names him, so they say nothing about his picks in particular. With no posts either way there is no smoke to report; there is simply very little talk. Our Reddit search was partial. The Reddit archive's full text search timed out on 17 Nov 2026, so we checked our saved copy of ten betting subreddits and one WagerTalk thread instead. None of them mentioned him.
CapperTek lists more than a dozen reviews of WagerTalk.com. The ones we read describe advertised records that did not hold up after purchase. None of them mentions Rob Veno.

TheRX daily service play threads tell members not to post picks from a list of services, and his name is on it. The thread gives no reason, and it is a forum rule, not a judgment on any one handicapper.
Web searches of Covers, Sportsbook Review, TheRX and general search results found no thread reviewing Rob Veno by name and no buyer posting a record of his paid picks.

conflicts: WagerTalk grades his picks, ranks him on its own leaderboards and sells his packages. The records on his profile therefore come from the seller's side of the deal.
He also co-hosts WagerTalk shows, such as Full Court Press with Adam Trigger, and the free picks and shows double as advertising for paid passes.
strengths: Sold through a company with a Las Vegas mailing address and written terms.
Every package has a published price, and his bio gives a long, specific public history in Las Vegas betting media.
He posts free picks with written reasoning, and the profile shows a Last 20 table that includes losses.
concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw is a run over a window chosen by the seller, or a ranking on WagerTalk's own board.
The guarantee pays in site credit, only on daily packages, never in cash. All sales are final.
We found no independent buyer reports, positive or negative, about his paid picks.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and free days. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits or more picks.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real, active WagerTalk handicapper with published prices, free picks and a company address behind the sales, and a long history on Las Vegas betting radio. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because the only records on show are graded by WagerTalk itself, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
How much does Rob Veno cost?

On 17 Nov 2026 passes ran $39.00 for a day, $99.00 for a week, $299.00 for 30 days and $1,999.00 for a year. Season passes ran from $259.00 to $719.00, prop passes $199.00 or $499.00, and a one payment year promotion was $1,188.
Does Rob Veno have a verified record?

No. His profile shows runs such as +69.7 units at 82-56-0 over nine weeks and a Last 20 table of 14 wins and 6 losses on 17 Nov 2026, all graded by WagerTalk. We found no independent, time stamped log of every pick.

For the money you get every play he releases in the period you buy, with written analysis. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays, the guarantee only gives site credit on daily picks, and nothing refunds your betting losses.
